samples.summary: `usedControls` carries no per-entry provenance (`sha`), breaking the file's own stated "STALENESS IS PER ENTRY" design principle
samples.evidence: The module header (lines 36–42) states the design rule: "STALENESS IS PER ENTRY... every entry carries the tree it was observed at and the renderer marks the stale ones individually", and "Under-warning is the failure that costs a missed defect". Every other persisted collection follows it — `shapes`, `pairs`, `readAfterMutation` and `inventory` all carry a `sha` and `stale()` renders a marker. The new `usedControls` is a bare sorted string array with no sha, and it is carried across every key bump forever (mergeCoverage line 401-408). Because `untried = inventory.filter(x => !usedControls.has(x.control))` (line 496), a control clicked once forty commits ago is now permanently suppressed from the "NEVER TRIED" section with no staleness signal at all — precisely the under-warning direction the design says is the costly one. The equivalent `inventory` carry-across at least preserved `{role, control, sha}`.

samples.summary: After a key bump, a control in `usedControls` but with no surviving shape entry disappears from the brief entirely — it is neither offered as untried nor listed as applied/round-tripped
samples.evidence: renderCoverageBrief builds its "Already ROUND-TRIPPED" and "Applied but NEVER REVERSED" sections from `shapes` only (lines 445-446), which a bump empties. The new `usedControls` only subtracts from `untried` (line 496). Net effect of the change on a freshly bumped memory: those controls vanish from the brief — the explorer is told nothing about them, neither "try this" nor "you already did this on shape X". The stated outcome ("untried stays honest") is met, but the memory the brief conveys for those controls is silence rather than the honest "clicked before, shape unknown, depth unexplored" that would steer the next run.

samples.summary: The persisted coverage-memory schema gains a new field with no design-doc update; Phase 31 / hunter-usage.md do not record the record shape or the key-bump carry-across rules
samples.evidence: Phase 31 (docs/design/harness-engineering.md:2902+) documents the UI hunter in detail but never describes the coverage record's fields, and docs/design/hunter-usage.md:112-124 mentions `--coverage` only operationally. This change alters the on-disk memory format (a new top-level `usedControls` array) and introduces a second field with bump-survival semantics distinct from the version gate; all of that rationale lives only in source comments. CONTRIBUTING's design-doc discipline would put it in the canonical Phase 31 subsystem doc. Confidence is low because the pre-existing `inventory` carry-across was likewise documented only in code, so the repo's de facto convention for this module may be code-comment-only.
searchedFor: glob docs/design/**/*.md for a coverage-memory doc

samples.summary: `usedControls` is redundant state derivable from `shapes` in the same record, creating two places that must agree
samples.evidence: coverageFromJournal derives it from `shapes` (line 286) while mergeCoverage recomputes it as a union of both records' `usedControls` and both records' `shapes` (lines 401-408). The comment acknowledges the redundancy and justifies it by bump-survival; an alternative with no duplicated state would have been to derive the carry-across inside mergeCoverage from `prev.shapes` alone (which it already does) and keep the field out of the written record. That variant fails only on a second consecutive bump, the case the new test at hunt-ui-coverage.test.mjs:217 covers — so the redundancy is defensible, but it is genuinely duplicated state and worth naming.

verdict.reason: Verified in the working tree, not taken on trust. The header invariant is real and quoted accurately (hunt-ui-coverage.mjs:36-42). Every other persisted collection carries per-entry provenance — shapes (259, 287), pairs (288), readAfterMutation (289-291), inventory (292-297) — and mergeCoverage preserves sha per entry (323-328, 340, 355) so stale() (442) can mark them. `usedControls` alone is a bare sorted string array with no sha (286) and is merged from `prev`/`next` directly rather than the version-gated a/b (401-408), so it survives every COVERAGE_KEY_VERSION bump permanently and is structurally incapable of ever being stale-marked. It feeds the untried filter at 490-496, which drives the "NEVER TRIED" section (516-529) that the file itself calls "the most valuable thing here" — so a control clicked once at an old tree is suppressed forever with no staleness signal, the exact under-warning direction lines 40-42 name as the costly failure. No guard exists: hunt-ui.mjs:1155-1172 loads the coverage file and normalises it through mergeCoverage(null, record), the very path that carries usedControls across untouched, and there is no age or sha based pruning anywhere. The .trusted baseline (line 459) computed usedControls locally from shapes with no persisted field, so this provenance-free permanent state is newly shaped here. This is a data-model/approach-fit inconsistency with the module's own stated design rule (wrong abstraction for a persisted collection), which is in the design-fit lane rather than a line-level logic bug. The file's own counter-rationale at 280-285 and 388-400 ("this control has been clicked never stops being true") is a genuine design tension with the header's "already covered describes a tree", but that is a disagreement to resolve, not a refutation. None of not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope applies.
